html:
A king of Sparta who led the Greek force that held the pass of Thermopylae against the Persian army of Xerxes I in 480 BCE, and died there.

He was a son of King Anaxandridas II and came to the throne around 490 BCE. When Xerxes invaded Greece, the allied Greeks sent a small army north to block the narrow coastal road at Thermopylae, while their fleet fought nearby at Artemisium. For two days they held off the Persians. Then a local man showed the Persians a mountain path around the pass. Leonidas sent most of the allies away and stayed with his 300 Spartans and some other Greeks, and almost all were killed.

The Battle of Thermopylae was a defeat, and the Persians went on to burn Athens. But it became a lasting symbol of courage, made famous by Herodotus. The Greeks won the war weeks later at sea at Salamis, under Themistocles, and on land at Plataea in 479 BCE.
sum: A king of Sparta who led the Greek force that held the pass of Thermopylae against the Persian army of Xerxes I in 480 BCE, and died there.
